articles.title: Andy Dalton Reportedly Released by Eagles After Cam Jurgens Trade, Lane Johnson's Retirement
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles released backup quarterback Andy Dalton on Friday, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles released backup quarterback Andy Dalton on Friday, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo .

Tanner McKee and Cole Payton now sit behind Jalen Hurts on Philadelphia's depth chart.

The Eagles' roster has undergone several changes as of late, with center Cam Jurgens getting traded to the Baltimore Ravens on Wednesday after right tackle Lane Johnson retired on Tuesday.

Stephen A. Apologizes After Lane Johnson Comments

As for Dalton, an eventual return to Philadelphia is a possibility.

The Eagles could still bring him back on their 53-man roster or practice squad, per Garafolo .

Dalton was in the midst of his first season in Philadelphia after spending the past three years as a depth option for the Carolina Panthers.

The 38-year-old suited up in three preseason contests for the Eagles, going 18-of-35 for 168 yards and one touchdown without getting picked off.

Dalton briefly appeared in Philadelphia's 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 3 as Hurts was being evaluated for a concussion , tossing an interception while the Eagles had the ball at Chicago's two-yard line.

Hurts returned to the game on the team's next drive.

The Eagles eventually promoted McKee to their second-string quarterback spot over Dalton on Sunday.

Despite the veteran's costly turnover, Philadelphia may value his experience and look to sign him again as it attempts to clinch a sixth consecutive playoff berth.

Dalton has started 169 games across his 16 seasons in the NFL from 2011-26, while McKee has just two starts under his belt. Payton, a fifth-round rookie, has yet to appear in a regular-season game.

articles.title: Travis Kelce joins Cleveland Guardians ownership group as $1.7 billion MLB franchise adds a new chapter to his hometown legacy
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has built a successful career in the NFL, but his interests now extend beyond football.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has built a successful career in the NFL, but his interests now extend beyond football. In May 2026, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end became a minority investor in the Cleveland Guardians, giving him a financial connection to the Major League Baseball team he grew up supporting. The investment brings his professional success closer to his hometown roots, but questions remain about how much he paid, what percentage he owns, and whether his involvement could influence the franchise’s future. While the financial details remain private, the deal offers an interesting look at how professional athletes are turning their earnings and public profiles into long-term business investments.What do we know about Travis Kelce’s investment in the Cleveland Guardians?The Cleveland Guardians announced Kelce’s minority investment on May 27, 2026, marking a new chapter in the relationship between the NFL star and his hometown. The announcement came before the team’s game against the Washington Nationals, bringing attention to a deal that connected one of football’s most recognizable players with Cleveland’s baseball franchise.Kelce purchased a minority interest from the ownership group associated with David Blitzer. Blitzer holds a 35% stake in the Guardians, making his position an important part of the team’s ownership structure. However, this does not mean Kelce purchased 35% of the franchise. The reported transaction involved a portion of Blitzer’s interest, and the exact percentage acquired by Kelce has not been publicly disclosed.The distinction matters because ownership percentages determine the financial value of an investment and the rights that come with it. Without knowing Kelce’s exact share, it is not possible to establish his ownership value, calculate his expected returns, or determine how much of the team’s business he owns.The purchase price has also remained private. Neither Kelce nor the Guardians has announced the amount paid for the investment. As a result, figures circulating about his personal spending should not be treated as confirmed unless they can be supported by reliable reporting or an official disclosure.The transaction nevertheless gives Kelce a direct financial interest in a major professional baseball franchise. Instead of simply attending games or supporting the team as a celebrity fan, he now has a business connection to the organization.For Cleveland, the investment also brings an internationally recognized sports personality closer to the Guardians brand. Kelce’s NFL career, public appearances, and business activities give him a profile that extends beyond football. His involvement can attract attention to the baseball team, although the actual financial impact of that attention cannot be measured from the ownership announcement alone.How much are the Cleveland Guardians worth, and what could Kelce’s stake be worth?The Guardians’ reported valuation provides useful context for understanding why the investment has attracted attention. Forbes estimated the franchise’s value at approximately $1.7 billion around the time of the announcement, with other reports placing the figure in a similar range. The valuation reflects the broader business value of the franchise, rather than the amount Kelce paid for his individual share.The Guardians were valued at approximately $1 billion in 2022, when Blitzer first invested in the organization. Comparing that figure with the later estimate of roughly $1.7 billion suggests a substantial increase in the franchise’s reported value over four years.That rise is significant because professional sports teams can become valuable long-term assets. Their businesses are supported by several sources of income, including broadcasting agreements, ticket sales, sponsorships, merchandise, stadium-related revenue, and other commercial partnerships. The exact mix varies by franchise, and a team’s overall valuation does not mean all of that value is immediately available as cash to its owners.A higher franchise valuation can benefit existing investors if they eventually sell their shares at a favorable price. However, an increase in estimated value does not automatically translate into a realized profit. The final return depends on the purchase price, ownership percentage, operating costs, financial obligations, and the terms of a future sale.For Kelce, the absence of a disclosed ownership percentage makes it impossible to calculate a reliable value for his investment. For example, a hypothetical 1% interest in a franchise valued at $1.7 billion would correspond to $17 million before considering transaction terms and other adjustments. That is only an illustration of the mathematics, not a claim that Kelce owns 1% or invested $17 million.The same caution applies to estimates of how much money he might earn from the deal. The Guardians have not disclosed Kelce’s investment terms, any special financial arrangements, or the returns he could receive. It would therefore be inaccurate to describe a particular amount as his confirmed investment or expected profit.The most reliable conclusion is that Kelce has acquired an undisclosed minority interest in a franchise whose reported value is around $1.7 billion. That makes the deal potentially significant, but its precise financial value to him remains unknown.Will Travis Kelce have any control over the Guardians’ players and baseball decisions?Kelce’s investment does not make him the person responsible for running the Cleveland Guardians. His position as a minority investor is different from the role of a controlling owner, team president, general manager, or manager. These positions carry different responsibilities, and owning a portion of a franchise does not automatically give an investor authority over its baseball operations.The Dolan family remains the Guardians’ controlling ownership group. Its position is important because control of a sports franchise generally determines who has the final say over major organizational decisions. Kelce’s reported investment does not replace the existing ownership structure or give him control over the team.Decisions involving player contracts, trades, recruitment, coaching appointments, payroll, and long-term baseball strategy remain matters for the organization’s established leadership. There is no confirmed information indicating that Kelce will have direct authority over these decisions.This distinction is especially important when a celebrity becomes involved with a sports franchise. The public may associate a famous investor with the team and assume that the person will influence its future. In reality, an investor’s involvement depends on the rights attached to the shares they purchase and the agreements governing the ownership group.The Guardians have also been connected to a separate ownership development involving Blitzer. His 35% interest comes with an option to pursue majority control after the 2027 season. However, an option is not the same as a completed transaction. It gives its holder a potential route to a future deal, subject to the applicable terms, rather than guaranteeing that control will change hands.Kelce’s investment should therefore be understood within the existing ownership arrangement. His financial interest connects him to the franchise, but there is no confirmed basis for saying he will decide which players the Guardians sign, how much they spend on their roster, or who leads their baseball operations.His most visible contribution may instead come through his public profile and relationship with the city. A well-known athlete supporting a local team can attract media coverage, strengthen community connections, and introduce the franchise to audiences who might not regularly follow baseball. Those possibilities make the investment interesting without requiring Kelce to take on a management role.Why does the Guardians investment matter to Kelce’s hometown and his growing business portfolio?For Kelce, the Guardians investment carries a personal connection that goes beyond the financial value of the franchise. He grew up in Northeast Ohio and attended Cleveland Heights High School, where baseball was part of his sporting background before football became the centre of his professional career.His connection to Cleveland has remained part of his public identity even after establishing himself with the Kansas City Chiefs. The investment gives him a way to maintain that connection while participating in the business side of professional sports.The Guardians described Kelce as someone with a deep affection for Cleveland and Northeast Ohio. Kelce, in turn, presented the opportunity as a chance to strengthen his lasting connection with the city’s east side. These statements help explain the personal meaning of the deal, although they do not reveal its financial terms.The investment also fits into Kelce’s wider business activities. Beyond his NFL career, he has developed commercial interests and partnerships in areas such as entertainment, consumer brands, and sports. His business portfolio has included ventures associated with Garage Beer, investments connected to entertainment and hospitality, and the New Heights podcast, which he co-hosts with his brother, Jason Kelce.These activities show how a professional athlete can build income sources and business relationships beyond a playing contract. An athlete’s career on the field is limited by factors such as age, performance, injuries, and contract opportunities. Investments, by contrast, can potentially continue to hold value after the athlete retires, although they also carry financial risks.Owning a minority share of a baseball franchise offers a different opportunity from endorsing a product. An endorsement generally involves promoting a brand in exchange for compensation, while an equity investment gives the investor an ownership interest in a business. The potential financial outcome depends on the business’s performance, the value of the shares, and the terms of the investment.There may also be a branding benefit for the Guardians. Kelce’s popularity gives the team a connection to a major NFL audience, while his hometown background makes the relationship more meaningful to local supporters. However, it would be premature to assign a specific financial benefit to his involvement without evidence of increased ticket sales, sponsorship revenue, merchandise purchases, or other measurable results.Ultimately, the investment is both a business decision and a personal milestone for Kelce. It connects his professional success to a city that played an important role in his development and adds another dimension to his activities outside football.The central facts remain straightforward. Kelce became a minority investor in the Cleveland Guardians in May 2026, but the size and price of his stake have not been disclosed. The franchise has been valued at approximately $1.7 billion, while the Dolan family continues to hold the controlling position. articles.title: 49ers' Kyle Juszczyk Posts Pokemon Football Lineup in Photo Amid Viral Trend, 'Low Man Wins'
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk joined in on the viral trend in which Pokémon are used to create a 22-man football lineup.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk joined in on the viral trend in which Pokémon are used to create a 22-man football lineup.

Juszczyk showcased his lineup in a Friday post on X while explaining that he used the Pokémon Dugtrio as his fullback because the "low man wins."

The 35-year-old is an avid Pokémon fan, bonding with 49ers teammate George Kittle over their shared hobby.

"Me and Juice both have a love, love, love for Pokémon," Kittle said on his podcast The Kittle Things in Nov. 2025 (21:53 mark). "An absolute infatuation."

"I don't think me and Juice even know we both loved Pokémon until probably 2019," he added. "We were just like, 'Wait, you like Pokémon?' Woah."

Juszczyk is in the midst of his 14th NFL season and his 10th with San Francisco.

The 10-time Pro Bowler has remained an important piece of a 49ers offense that ranks No. 2 in the NFL by averaging 30.5 points per game.

Juszczyk is currently dealing with a knee injury after appearing in each of San Francisco's first four contests, catching four passes for 55 yards and a touchdown.

articles.title: Cowboys' Schottenheimer Talks Potential Coaching Staff Changes, Says He'll 'Look at Everything'
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer discussed possible changes to the team's coaching staff on Friday.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer discussed possible changes to the team's coaching staff on Friday.

"I'm going to look at everything," Schottenheimer said, per Jon Machota of The Athletic. "I'll spend countless hours trying to figure it out and getting a chance to step back, look at these five games, and see what we need to improve."

He also detailed his plan for the weekend after the Cowboys suffered a 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night.

"This weekend is going to be a process," Schottenheimer said, per Machota. "We're going to go through the process. We're going to figure it out. We're going to watch the tape. We're going to look at the stats. We're going to look at everything and we're going to make some decisions that we believe will give us the best chance to pick back up and play well next week."

With the loss to Tampa Bay, Dallas fell to 2-3 to start the 2026 season.

The defeat was particularly disappointing considering the Buccaneers entered the game with an 0-4 record and were starting backup quarterback Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie.

During Daniels' first career start against the Green Bay Packers in Week 4, Tampa Bay only mustered 14 points and 275 total yards.

In his second start on Thursday, the Buccaneers amassed 419 yards to go along with their 24 points. Daniels finished 19-of-25 for 189 yards and one touchdown.

After consecutive seven-win seasons in 2024 and 2025, the Cowboys looked to establish themselves as a contender in the NFC East this year.

Instead, Dallas' defense has remained an issue. The Cowboys are giving up 27.2 points and 395.4 yards per game through five weeks.

While Dallas' offense has been largely productive, the unit has become increasingly one-dimensional. Schottenheimer's squad owns the NFL's No. 28 rushing attack , averaging a mere 81.6 yards per game on the ground.

If the Cowboys can't turn their season around quickly, coaching changes could be on the horizon.

articles.title: Andy Dalton In Line to End Up On Wrong Side of NFL History With Rare Stat After Eagles Release
articles.summary: Quarterback Andy Dalton could make NFL history if he doesn't throw another pass after his reported release by the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Quarterback Andy Dalton could make NFL history if he doesn't throw another pass after his reported release by the Philadelphia Eagles.

Dalton was picked off when attempting his lone pass attempt so far this season in a Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears.

He could now become the seventh quarterback to finish a season 0-for-1 with an interception if he doesn't see any more playing time this season, per the AP's Josh Dubow.

Dalton's interception took place on a red zone drive that took place while Jalen Hurts was undergoing a concussion check in the second quarter of the Week 3 loss.

The last player to achieve that season-long statline as a quarterback was Feleipe Franks with the Atlanta Falcons in 2021, per Dubow. Franks is currently playing as a tight end and special teamer for the Carolina Panthers.

There's still a chance Dalton could improve his passing rate this season. Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer tied Dalton's release to the Eagles' need for space on the 53-man roster, and noted the quarterback could potentially return as a practice squad member.

The Eagles traded a seventh-round pick to the Carolina Panthers last spring in order to acquire Dalton, who later won beat out Tanner McKee to begin the season as Philadelphia's QB2. McKee is now set to serve as Hurts' backup going forward.

articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Another Friday. We're here. We've made it! While the left spent all week whining about Sophie Cunningham's hat and firing squad best practices, us PATRIOTS were biding our time, keeping our heads down, and grinding towards another weekend. And now, we're here. And there ain't a thing they can do about it. Let's roll. Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham's ex-teammate, Sydney Colson, virtue-signals her BUTT off while also having maybe the worst career stats I've ever seen. SPORTS MEDIA OUTLET CONSIDERS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM MORE POLARIZING THAN MEGAN RAPINOE Seriously. This is who's telling Sophie — and white people — to shut up? The WNBA can do better than this, right? Right?! What else? I've got Dak getting heckled by an Uber driver, a referee absolutely trucking a poor soul on the sidelines, and I'm sad about Mike Ditka. What an awful year for deaths. I feel like we say that every year, but goodness, 2026 has been a real kick to the you-know-whats in terms of death. And we still have three months to go! Brutal. On that happy note, grab you a slice of sausage pizza ahead of Sunday's National Sausage Pizza Day, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap! This is the best they got? Really? I've got no real hot takes on pizza beyond the fact that I do, in fact, believe sausage is the best topping. I'm not just saying that because of the occasion. It's the best, by a mile. Mount Rushmore of Pizza Toppings to kick this Friday class off? Sure. Why not?! Meatballs as a topping are underrated in the pizza topping game. They're not on every menu, but when they are, HAMMER it. You are welcome! And that concludes our Ted Talk portion of today's class. NOW, let's officially get the day started with some ex-WNBA player named Sydney Colson pandering to the left by telling Sophie Cunningham and her white counterparts to PIPE DOWN. Amazing: At least she backed up her talk on the floor! Listen, if you never speak up about a d–n thing when you know it’s impacting the people that you claim to love, care about, you know we’re fighting together as a team, sister, blah blah blah, and you don’t speak up when things affect them. They don’t respect you. They are just trying to make it. Let me just tell you now, for real, for real: For the white players in the league, when you don’t say s–t, and even worse, when you say things that are harmful, talking about the trans s–t, nobody respects you. Shut the f–k up. Shut the f–k up. Nobody wants to hear your opinion. Freedom of speech, so you can say it, but just know people are just trying to get by when they’re dealing with you. And you ought to be ashamed. Y’all ought to be ashamed to act like you’re cool with people, to act like you care about sisterhood, all of these things. Again, it's just amazing. These "athletes" are just incredible. They're the gifts that keep on giving "the whole year," as Cousin Eddie would say. As Dan Z. said in the above post, let's quickly remind everyone of the VERY HARMFUL thing Sophie Cunningham told ESPN months ago as it pertains to trans people: "I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that.’ I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men." That's it! THAT's what Sydney Colson, who played with Cunningham last season in Indiana, deems "harmful" rhetoric. Speaking of last season, because I had never heard of this girl before this morning, I decided to do some Big J digging to see if her play on the court warranted all this chest-pumping off of it. It ... did not: Dak, Mike & what a hit! Well, there you have it. That's who is calling out Sophie Cunningham. A player who struggled to score three points per game during her illustrious career in the WNBA. Okeedokee! By the way, for the "Sophie stinks, too!" crowd ... she's averaged at least 8 points per game off the bench every year since 2022, including two seasons in double-digits. She's also a top-five three-point shooter in the league. It ain't close. OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL! To hype everyone up, let's start off with a ref in last night's South Alabama-Arkansas State game lowering his shoulder on a 100-yard kick return: BOOOOM! You don't often see a referee doing the trucking, right? Usually, we're watching those guys get pummeled. Frankly, it's a nice change of pace for the Zebras. I've spent all year ragging on them — for good reason. They've generally stunk at all levels. But credit where it's due here. This guy had a job to do, and he wasn't gonna let some innocent bystander stand in his way. Nicely done. Next? Speaking of (not so) innocent bystanders ... So, Dak and the Cowboys put up their annual primetime clunker last night, and this was the big story that came out of it ... Someone — boots on the ground say the guy was a driver — called Dak "embarrassing" after he threw two picks in a loss to the winless Buccaneers, and he took exception to it. I say fair on both accounts, by the way. The guy was pissed. He was clearly a fan. Dak stunk. It was embarrassing. Dak also has a right to turn his head around and get pissed. I would, too. And if the guy really did turn his head around after saying it, and then doubled down AFTER Dak looked away, it is kind of a wussy move. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! If you're gonna say something, say it! Don't be a keyboard warrior. Man up, call Dak out for his stinker, and let the chips fall where they may. OK, that's it for today — and this week. Good work, everyone. Solid week. And now we get to enjoy three straight nights of football. What a blessing. What a country. articles.title: Shocking suspensions, f-bombs and a flurry of flags. What's going on with NFL officiating and what's next?
articles.summary: The league pressed the officiating union for more accountability measures ahead of the new CBA. And the league just suspended two officials a full eight seas...
articles.body:
With 1:48 to play in the first half of the New England Patriots-Buffalo Bills game on Sunday, the officiating crew made an announcement.

"Unsportsmanlike conduct, head coach for New England."

The Bills were awarded half the distance to the goal in yardage that would set them up for a game-tying touchdown less than a minute later.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, upon hearing the officials, looked taken aback. Penalty yards for telling the official that a defensive holding flag was a "f***ing terrible f***ing call"?

"I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach," Vrabel said after the Patriots' 29-26 win . "There was nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive …

"I probably shouldn't have swore. But I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that."

By day's end, the comments of Vrabel — one of six head coaches currently serving on the NFL's competition committee — would take on heightened import.

Because across the league, tension between officials and players hit a rare high last week. Line judge Jeff Seeman, in view of a broadcasting camera, told Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride "f*** you." Referee Adrian Hill appeared to motion demonstratively and emotionally at Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson after a tangle with Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon knocked Wilson into Hill, who fell to the ground. (Wilson appeared to offer Hill a hand to get up.)

The suspensions, against the backdrop of Vrabel's public comments that he has regularly used profanity in interacting with officials, beg the question: What is the threshold of acceptable conduct from officials toward players and coaches, and in reverse? How should the system work and what explains the seeming increase in tension through the NFL's first four weeks?

Yahoo Sports canvassed league sources to better understand the dynamic of an often-charged relationship that seems tenser than usual. What awaits the rest of the season?

"It's a really tough job to be a ref," Pittsburgh Steeler wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. told Yahoo Sports by Zoom this week . "They take a lot of verbal abuse from coaches, players, fans. So definitely it's not for the thin-skinned."

After refs union calls suspension 'excessive and inconsistent,' league sources reiterate 'expectation' for officials in heated moments

It's impossible to determine how and whether contentious collective bargaining agreement (CBA) negotiations between the NFL and officials this spring have trickled over into the early weeks of the season.

Ask some team and league executives, and they'll say it's coincidence that these suspensions occurred the same week and coincidence this timed with multiple high-profile coaches questioning officiating.

Ask others, and the proximity of this tension to the league threatening replacement officials seems "impossible" to deny, in the word of one NFC executive.

What is clear: The league pressed the officiating union for more accountability measures ahead of the new CBA. And the league just suspended two officials a full eight seasons after the last known officiating suspension.

Before this week, the last known officiating suspension (officially an "administrative leave") was Roy Ellison's 2018 due to an official-player confrontation. Side judge Rob Vernatchi was suspended one game in 2015 due to a game-clock error, and Ellison was also suspended one game in 2013 after profanity against a player. Before that, the last suspension dated back to 1984 in response to an official's conduct toward fans.

So suspending two officials in a season, much less in one week, is unusual.

The officiating union issued a Tuesday statement saying it would "challenge the severity of those suspensions and meet with the NFL Officiating Department to discuss the League's disciplinary standards."

"NFL officials have a responsibility to conduct themselves professionally on the field, and the actions in these incidents fell short of that standard," NFL Referees Association executive director Scott Green said. "Accountability matters, but that should not result in discipline that is excessive or inconsistent with established precedent."

Coaches and players can, via flag and fine, receive discipline for their words and actions toward officials. This most often occurs if a player or coach repeatedly tests the boundaries with an official in a game, officials often warning coaches or players before issuing more discipline.

League sources do not believe frustration with a player or coach warrants a heated response.

"If they think somebody crosses the line, then they can drop the flag," one league source with knowledge of officiating discussions told Yahoo Sports. "Ultimately, the expectation is that these guys should not be in altercations and should walk away from it."

Neither Seeman nor Hill did that. Add to that bye weeks reducing the number of officials needed in Week 5 and Week 6 relative to the first four weeks, and the officiating bench now offering a deeper roster since the signing of the CBA, and the league chose to act at a rate it hasn't in league history.

Less-drastic accountability, league sources say, is not unusual. Each week, each official is graded not only on the consistency and accuracy of their calls, but also on behavioral considerations such as their field positioning, administration, mechanics, communication and speed. Those grades influence playoff assignments, with the most successful officials earning the highest-profile and most-coveted matchups. (The union sought to negotiate playoff assignments based on seniority rather than performance in the spring, and the league did not budge.)

Some coaches and players approach officials before a game to discuss their top concerns about their opponents' flag worthiness as well as ask for clarity on how a call will be officiated. Others try to minimize their interactions with officials and hope for the best.

"I don't like to talk to the refs," Pittman said, speaking in partnership with Toyota NFL FLAG. "They make me mad. When I was a younger player, I used to bark at them. But I always found that to come back and bite me.

"So now I just bite my tongue. I don't say anything."

Sources split on best response to rash of flags, high-profile calls

There are times, as it relates to officiating, that coaches and players are instructed not to say anything.

A defensive pass interference call in the final two minutes of the Los Angeles Rams' loss to the Denver Broncos brought that conversation back into public focus.

With 1:15 to play in the fourth quarter, Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was called for pass interference on a Bo Nix pass intended for Pat Bryant. The Broncos scored the game-winning touchdown after the drive stayed alive, and officials told Rams head coach Sean McVay in the days that followed that they agreed Wallace did not actually commit pass interference. McVay acknowledged that admission after he was asked about it multiple times during his news conference that week.

The league responded by sending a memo to teams reminding them conversations on officiating reviews are expected to be confidential.

"If something's obvious and the whole world wants to know 'hey, what ultimately happened?' then you've got to address it …" a high-ranking NFC executive told Yahoo Sports." But rehashing, that'd be like saying, 'OK, we're going to go over every grade of every player in the NFL last weekend and we're going to show it to the fans.' Is that transparency? I don't know.

McVay said he was focused more on the coaching point moving forward.

"The only thing that matters to me is how to educate our players," said McVay, who is also on the competition committee. "What I am interested in is if there's any sort of feedback that says this is in alignment with what would be correctly officiated as a DPI?

"That's the only thing that I'm really worried about."

League sources were split on whether there's reason to worry more broadly about officiating calls and conduct as Week 5 is underway.

On one hand, per ESPN data , the NFL saw the most accepted penalties through four weeks since play-by-play data became available in 1978. The 271 accepted penalties in Week 4 marked the second-most of any week in that span, per ESPN.

Others in the league counter that measuring "accepted" penalties rather than called penalties skews officials' performances. After all, officials don't choose whether to accept penalties. And some accepted penalties, like delay of game, can reflect strategy rather than overzealous officiating.

Delay of game and false start penalties are each at 10-year highs, per NFL data . More than half of the 63 delay-of-game penalties are on fourth down, when teams strategically prompt it, while an uptick in false starts could reflect the increased use of presnap motion by league offenses. The decrease in preseason participation by starters also has led to some less-disciplined play in recent years.

"You can't look at one penalty in abstract," a high-ranking team executive countered when told this information. "You have to look at game flow and what's actually being called and what's determining it. Because ultimately, that's what people were responding to."

NFL team owners and executives will meet Oct. 20 and 21 in New York City to discuss a range of issues with an agenda that historically has included officiating updates. It's rare any officiating or rule changes would occur during the season, though the NFL and NFL Players Association have already worked to clarify and reduce touchdown celebration penalties after a rash of fines.

Solutions league sources are interested in exploring: grant coaches one challenge flag to be used on currently unreviewable calls like defensive pass interference; issue two-minute reports of late-game officiating like the NBA does; allow broadcasts to stream the audio of officiating conversations as NCAA and UFL games do.

NBA and MLB each allow a coach's/manager's challenge per game, with stipulations; NHL allows coaching challenges as well albeit with penalty for incorrect challenges.

In the short term, it's unlikely any changes will occur. Multiple league sources predicted these suspensions, paired with the typical adjustment of players and coaches as a season elapses, will be enough to return officiating to perhaps not popular levels but at least normal ones.

Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur and Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell each expressed a desire to move past the incidents between their respective players and officials. LaFleur added that "I do want to give the man a little bit of grace."

Vrabel knows he, too, will need to watch his language and positioning after referee Bill Vinovich told a pool reporter that Vrabel leaving the box and cursing prompted "pretty much a given" penalty.

"I apologized to him," Vrabel said. "Again, players responded [to the penalty yardage]. It was unfortunate. And I have to be better in those moments."

articles.title: Eagles rule out RB Saquon Barkley, WR DeVonta Smith, along with member of new-look OL, ahead of London game vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: Across the pond, Philadelphia will be down its leading rusher and receiver, plus its new center.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles will be playing in a different country Sunday with a vastly different offensive lineup than the one they trotted out for Week 1 last month.

Against the 3-1 Jacksonville Jaguars in London this weekend, the 2-2 Eagles will be without their leading rusher and receiver, as well as a member of their new-look offensive line. Running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith will be sidelined with hamstring injuries. Due to a knee issue, Drew Kendall, who started the past three games at center, also won't be able to play.

Wideout Hollywood Brown (ankle) is also out and so is safety Marcus Epps (groin). Edge rusher Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is questionable.

On the bright side for the Eagles, they're getting tight end Dallas Goedert and linebacker Zack Baun back. Goedert missed the last two outings with a knee problem. A concussion kept Baun from competing in last week's loss to the Los Angeles Rams .

Still, the pressure will be on quarterback Jalen Hurts to generate offense despite key losses. After all, Philadelphia's offensive line has morphed midseason, particularly this week.

Six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson suddenly retired on Tuesday . On Wednesday, the Eagles traded two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens for draft compensation , namely a 2028 second-round pick. Jurgens had been filling in at left guard in the absence of three-time Pro Bowler Landon Dickerson, who went on injured reserve with a knee issue after the season opener .

Kendall, meanwhile, took Jurgens' place at center. His performance there has impressed general manager Howie Roseman . But the 2025 fifth-round pick from Boston College won't be available Sunday against the Jags.

That means Philadelphia will be missing three of its O-line starters from Weeks 2-3.

Former undrafted free agent Jake Majors, a second-year Texas product, appeared to be filling Kendall's void during practice Thursday, as captured by ESPN's Tim McManus . Majors was signed to the Eagles' active roster from their practice squad Friday.

Another undrafted player from the 2025 class is expected to slot in at left guard for the time being: Willie Lampkin.

Lampkin could be a short-term solution at the position until Dickerson returns from IR. Johnson's heir at right tackle is rookie Markel Bell, a third-rounder Philadelphia selected out of Miami.

The Eagles' transformed O-line will be blocking for not only Hurts but also a backfield that'll be down Barkley, as well as backup running back Tank Bigsby , the latter of whom landed on IR and needed core muscle surgery.

Will Shipley will likely be in for an increased workload on the ground. He'll be joined by a pair of practice squad backs: Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele. They've been elevated this week.

Pierce's presence in the league has faded in recent years, but he rushed for 939 yards as a rookie with the Houston Texans in 2022. As for Steele, he made three starts for the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024 and wrapped that season with 183 yards on 56 totes.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 5
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens will be without their quarterback for one of Week 5's highest-profile games.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will be without their quarterback for one of Week 5's highest-profile games.

Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's clash with the Atlanta Falcons due to an ankle injury he suffered in Week 4.

The injury news is a bit more optimistic elsewhere in the AFC North. Ja'Marr Chase is listed as questionable for the Cincinnati Bengals' matchup with the Miami Dolphins.

Below is a look at all of the significant injury news affecting fantasy football matchups in Week 5.

Lamar Jackson Ruled Out With Ankle Injury

Lamar Jackson is unable to go against the Falcons on Sunday night due to his ankle injury.

The news is concerning for the Ravens, their fans and fantasy football players with Jackson on their roster because his absence significantly alters the matchup.

Tyler Huntley is no stranger to starting games in place of Jackson. He went 8-for-9 for 63 yards last week, but the Ravens didn't score a second half point against the Tennessee Titans with Huntley on the field.

Huntley threw for 186 and 107 yards in his two starts last season. He led the Ravens to wins in both of those games, but the stat lines weren't overly impressive from a fantasy perspective.

It's difficult to justify Huntley as the first option off the waiver wire in place of Jackson because of those numbers and the state of the Ravens offense.

Zay Flowers is listed as questionable and Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews were both on the injury report this week. Bateman and Andrews were full participants in practice on Thursday and Friday.

A heavy reliance on Derrick Henry would be expected without Jackson, but Atlanta has given up the fewest rushing yards in the NFL through four weeks.

The waiver wire has a handful of non-Ravens who are better options to replace Jackson.

Arizona's Jacoby Brissett faces Detroit's league-worst passing defense. Aaron Rodgers might not be the first option, but the Pittsburgh Steelers are facing a brutal Indianapolis Colts secondary that struggled at points against Athan Kaliakmanis in London last week.

Jameis Winston is worth a look as well since he and the New York Giants go up against a Washington Commanders defense that's tied with Detroit and Arizona for the touchdowns conceded through the air.

Ja'Marr Chase Questionable For Bengals' Trip to Miami

Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals have one of the better matchups on paper in Week 5 against the Dolphins.

Miami gave up 24 or more points in its first three games and gave up over 330 total yards in three of its last four.

Chase left Week 4's game with the Jacksonville Jaguars due to a concussion. There was real concern about his Week 5 status, but he was a full participant in Friday's practice.

Tee Higgins is also listed as questionable, but like Chase, he was a full participant in practice on Friday.

A fully-functional Bengals offense has the potential to do a ton of damage against the Dolphins defense.

Chase, Higgins, Joe Burrow and Co. put up at least 350 total yards in three of their first four games. Another high yardage total is expected against a Miami defense with its bad yardage concession numbers.

If, for some reason, Chase can't go, Dohnte Meyers and Mike Gesicki would be popular waiver-wire additions at wide receiver, tight end and the FLEX spots because of upgraded roles inside the Bengals offense.

However, it looks like Chase is on track to play, and with that, will likely come a sizable fantasy point total.

articles.title: Kyle Monangai Injury, Latest News on Bears RB's Status & Fantasy Implications for Week 5 vs. Packers
articles.summary: Kyle Monangai is in the middle of a breakout season, but unfortunately the Chicago Bears running back will not be on the field for a Week 5 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Kyle Monangai is in the middle of a breakout season, but unfortunately the Chicago Bears running back will not be on the field for a Week 5 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Friday that Monangai has been ruled out with a toe injury. His injury is a "bigger concern" than Chicago initially believed, per ESPN's Courtney Cronin.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Thursday that Monangai is dealing with a turf toe injury that he was hoping to play through. Fowler added that his availability over the next one-to-two weeks was uncertain.

Monangai, who is in his second NFL season, has had a tremendous start to the 2026 campaign, rushing for 324 yards, the seventh-best mark in the league, along with three touchdowns on 60 carries. His 5.4 yards per carry ranks sixth in the NFL this season.

He's coming off a 146-yard, two-touchdown performance in a 23-12 win against the New York Jets on Sunday.

Monangai missing this week has fantasy implications too, as managers will now need to pick up a replacement.

One option that could still be available is the Chargers' Keaton Mitchell, who has been getting increasingly more touches throughout the season. Philadelphia's Will Shipley also has the chance to get more action this week since Saquon Barkley is week-to-week and Tank Bigsby is set to undergo core muscle surgery .

While the Bears will be without Monangai, the good news is they have another strong backfield option with D'Andre Swift.

Swift, who is in his third season in Chicago, has rushed for 311 yards and three touchdowns through four games. Unfortunately for the Bears, Swift is questionable heading into Sunday's game because of hip and knee injuries. He did not practice on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday.

The two backfield injuries come amid a hamstring injury to star quarterback Caleb Williams. The third-year player suffered the injury in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings and has missed the last two weeks.

Johnson said earlier this week that Tyson Bagent would once again be the starter for Chicago as Williams works his way back to the field.

Even with Williams missing the past two weeks, the Bears have gotten off to a 3-1 start as they look to get back to the playoffs following a strong 2025 campaign. Chicago will look to pick up a rivalry win on Sunday, but the status of its running backs is a big factor in whether it can leave Lambeau Field victorious.

articles.title: Browns Called Top Trade Destination for 1,000-Yard Bucs RB
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns called top trade destination for Bucs' 1,000-yard running back. The post Browns Called Top Trade Destination for 1,000-Yard Bucs RB appeared...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers signed free-agent running back Kenneth Gainwell as an expensive alternative to presumed starter Bucky Irving after injury issues kept him sidelined for most of 2025.

Irving has come out of the gate looking like one of the NFL's best running backs—just like his rookie year in 2024—while Gainwell has largely been an afterthought on a 2-year, $14 million contract.

Bleacher Report's Alex Ballentine thinks that if the Buccaneers continue to spiral after a 1-4 start, Gainwell could be an attractive trade option for a playoff hopeful.

In this case, a surprise playoff hopeful — the Cleveland Browns.

"Targeting secondary backs who help in the passing game," Ballentine wrote on October 9. "Targeting Kenneth Gainwell would just be a more experienced version of that kind of back."

Gainwell had over 1,000 yards of total offense with the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2025.

Kenneth Gainwell Called NFL's Top Backup RB

ESPN's Bill Barnwell put Gainwell at the top of his list of the NFL's top backup running backs in the preseason.

"One of 2025's most productive backs on a per-touch basis, Gainwell averaged 4.7 yards per carry on the ground and caught 73 passes as an outlet for Aaron Rodgers ," Barnwell wrote on July 20. "He was sixth in the NFL in success rate (47.4%) among RBs with 100 or more carries, while his explosive play rate (9.6%) was right around league average. He is another back perfectly suited for a rotational role, and he'll compete with Dowdle to be our RB1."

Kenneth Gainwell Made Big Offseason Impression

Following Tampa Bay's mandatory minicamp, Pewter Report's Bailey Adams singled out Gainwell as a player who jumped off the page.

"Veteran running back Kenny Gainwell, a newcomer to the Bucs offense, was a major standout," Adams wrote on June 18. "During 7-on-7 work, he caught a fade for a touchdown from Baker Mayfield , going up to make a leaping catch before falling to the ground and securing the ball … getting a lot of the reps with the starters due to Bucky Irving's recovery from injury, Gainwell shined both as a runner and as a pass catcher. But it was his work in the passing game that stood out the most. It really looks like he'll be a big part of the passing game under new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson."

Irving was a sensation as a rookie, with 1,514 yards of total offense and 8 touchdowns, including 1,122 rushing yards, while serving mostly as a backup to Rachaad White .

In 2025, Irving had 865 total yards and 4 touchdowns.

articles.title: Seahawks have a fun challenge on their hands with 49ers' Brock Purdy
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks and the San Francisco 49ers are gearing up for a high-contest game.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks are trying hard to get back to the big game and be one of the new NFL franchises to notch back-to-back championship wins, and so far, they're 3-1, so they're getting there. But they obviously have a challenge up against the San Francisco 49ers .

The 49ers are undefeated going into Week 5, and they're No. 1 in the NFC West. There's no denying that quarterback Brock Purdy is just playing good football, and that's tough to top. But the Seahawks can do it, and one way is by finally sacking Purdy.

In a Friday feature, ESPN released its predictions for the NFL Week 5 schedule of games. In it, they mention a fun fact that Purdy actually has yet to be sacked this season. So, consider it a fun challenge for the Seahawks' defense to be the first to sack him.

Brock Purdy has yet to be sacked this season

"When the Seahawks beat the 49ers in Week 18 and in the divisional round of the playoffs last season, their defense held San Francisco to a combined 409 yards and nine points," Brady Henderson of ESPN notes. "That was then. The 49ers' offense now? Second in the NFL in scoring at 30.5 points per game, and QB Brock Purdy has yet to take a sack."

Ahead of the Seahawks and 49ers game, Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald said of Purdy, "He can throw at all three levels. He throws on time. He throws it into windows with timing that makes it hard to defend."

Listen, so long as nobody gets hurt, sacking the other team's quarterback is a good thing. So, perhaps the Seahawks will be the first team in the 2026-27 season to do so.

articles.title: Davis Webb Reacts to Playcalling Demotion as Sean Payton Takes Over Amid Broncos Struggles
articles.summary: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton handed over play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Davis Webb this offseason, but he has taken them back after four games.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton handed over play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Davis Webb this offseason, but he has taken them back after four games.

On Friday, reporters asked Webb whether a four-game sample size was enough to judge whether a change was needed, per ESPN's Jeff Legwold .

"Luckily that's not my job, that's [Payton's] job," Webb said. "I think he answered that. I think the world of him, how we've gone about it ... it's not ideal, but in the same breath, we're 2-2 in the first four games, our first four opponents were a combined 13-3 to start the season. Welcome to the league."

It's clear Webb isn't happy with the change (and rightfully so), and he added further comments on the matter.

"Any time it happens in any aspect of your life jobwise [there's disappointment], but in the same breath that's the NFL, you get going," Webb said. "Been a backup QB, been up and down before, that's kind of how it goes."

Webb also spoke about what he learned in his four weeks as a playcaller.

In fairness to Webb, the Broncos had a brutal start to the season against the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs, 3-1 Jacksonville Jaguars, 2-2 Los Angeles Rams and 4-0 San Francisco 49ers.

The Rams, 49ers and Chiefs are second, third and eighth in fewest yards allowed per play, respectively, per Pro Football Reference . Jacksonville is 29th in that realm, but the Jags have also allowed the second-fewest points per game in the league (13.3).

Denver hasn't enjoyed a great offensive start so far. The Broncos are 27th in scoring and 25th in yards per play. They've been slow-starters all season, scoring just 13 points over four first halves. Denver has done much better in the second halves (61 points).

Quarterback Bo Nix has only passed for 5.8 adjusted yards per attempt (down from 6.4 in 2025) and 204.8 yards per game overall (down from 231.2 the prior year). The run game has been quiet, with rushers combining for 3.6 yards per carry (down from 4.4).

The 2-2 Broncos have treaded water so far, but Payton thought a change was needed now.

We'll see how the switch affects Denver soon enough when the Broncos visit the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET.

As for Webb, the coaching future should still be bright for him. At just 31 years old, the former backup QB (six seasons) has risen quickly through the Broncos' coaching ranks, first as a QB coach (2023-2024) and then an offensive pass game coordinator in addition to QB coach duties (2025). He received a promotion to OC this offseason.

articles.title: At least one person isn't concerned about Cam Skattebo getting injured, and his name is Cam Skattebo

articles.title: Browns' Todd Monken Reveals Honest Quote From Jets Exec After 2019 HC Interview
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken disclosed the message that he received from a New York Jets executive after interviewing for the team's head coaching vacancy in 2019.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken disclosed the message that he received from a New York Jets executive after interviewing for the team's head coaching vacancy in 2019.

"Actually, someone from the Jets organization told me this now that I'm going to mention it," Monken told reporters Friday (0:07 mark). "It was one of the guys that were in the interview process and he said, 'Don't ever forget that you're a Mercedes. When you look in the mirror, you can't control if they want a Lexus.'"

"That doesn't mean you're not capable," he added. "It's like all of us when you go through interviews. You go through certain stages and you're like, 'You know what? There's things I certainly could have improved, interview and all those things. But ultimately, they chose a different model, and that was their choice.'"

NFL Insiders Talk Potential HC Candidates

The Jets ended up hiring Adam Gase as their head coach in 2019.

Gase was eventually fired after compiling a 9-23 record across two seasons with the team.

At the time Monken interviewed for the Jets' job opening, he was coming off his third consecutive season as offensive coordinator of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The Buccaneers owned the NFL's No. 12 scoring offense during their 2018 campaign with Monken, averaging 24.8 points per game.

After New York brought in Gase, Monken was hired by the Browns as their offensive coordinator in 2019.

He spent one season in Cleveland before joining Georgia as the school's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, remaining with the Bulldogs from 2020-22.

Monken eventually returned to the NFL level in 2023, becoming offensive coordinator of the Baltimore Ravens. He helped the Ravens put together several high-powered offenses during his tenure, including a 2024 squad that averaged a league-leading 424.9 total yards per game.

Monken stayed with Baltimore for three seasons until he was hired as head coach of the Browns on Jan. 28.

Cleveland has opened its 2026 campaign on a high note, sitting at 3-1 after posting a 5-12 record last year.

The Browns' offense has steadily progressed this season, as their scoring total has increased with each week. This includes a 27-point performance in a Week 4 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

As for the Jets, they're currently in their second year with Aaron Glenn patrolling the sidelines. New York owns a 4-17 record under Glenn, while the team has gone 1-3 over its first four games in 2026.

The Browns and Jets are set to face off on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Ayra Starr on her NFL history-making half-time show
articles.summary: The Nigerian star will become the first African artist to headline the show at an international NFL game.
articles.body:
Afrobeats singer Ayra Starr has already broken numerous records, and her NFL half-time performance this weekend is set to level up her list again.

The Nigerian star will become the first African artist to headline one of the American football league's international games when the Philadelphia Eagles take on the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

Ahead of the performance at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Starr told BBC Newsbeat her history-making performance "itself is a message".

Earlier this year, Puerto Rican superstar Bad Bunny used his Super Bowl half-time show to celebrate Latin American culture.

The 32-year-old also made history by becoming the first musician to perform entirely in Spanish at the sporting event, normally the most-watched each year on US TV.

Starr said it's "very important" for singers to seize opportunities like this.

"At the end of the day, as artists, we speak for the culture and we speak for the people that listen to us," she added.

"And we have to represent any way that seems fit, that they need."

She didn't want to give away too much about her performance, but confirmed it would feature tracks from her new studio album, Starrgirl, which was released in August.

"I'm still in rehearsals. It's a lot of work we're putting in so I'm really excited."

The 24-year-old has been making waves in recent years, becoming the first African woman to win best international act at the Mobo Awards and the first Nigerian woman to surpass one billion video views on YouTube.

But before she became a superstar, the singer studied for a degree in political sciences and international relations - and said this has influenced her work.

"When it comes to matters of women and equality and the girl child and even just children - I'm very outspoken on any platform that sees fit.

"Even with my music, my music is very much like 'I will do what I want' and freedom."

The Afrobeats genre, which originates from West Africa, has massively grown in recent years - dominating playlists and seeing artists, including Starr, featuring at major festivals such as Glastonbury.

She said the rest of the world is just "catching up" to a style that's been "popping in Africa for the longest time".

The singer added that becoming one of the dominant faces of the music she grew up listening to, alongside artists such as Wizkid and Burna Boy, is "crazy".

Starr acknowledged it's a male-dominated field and would like female artists to have more "space in the genre" and be "allowed the same privileges".

But she also feels this is just the beginning.

"Afrobeats just keeps evolving, it keeps growing and it just keeps getting better... I want it to be one of the top genres in the world."

articles.body:
Daniel Jeremiah of NFL Network believes Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker is the "most intriguing" quarterback in the 2027 NFL draft class.

Jeremiah said the following in response to a question from Rich Eisen, who asked the analyst who he felt (at this time) would be the first quarterback taken off the board in the 2027 NFL draft (4:20 mark).

"Where we are right now, I think the most intriguing player when you put all that stuff together would be Mestemaker," Jeremiah began.

"Just off early season here. Dante Moore, obviously he's hurt, hopefully he's OK after that horrendous hit that he took, but he has not played his best ball. They were on the same field, I watched that tape, and from an NFL standpoint, Mestemaker was just so much more intriguing with the athleticism that he has to go along with the other array of skills.

"In an ideal world for him and his development, just more playing time, another year would be great. But in terms of where we are at this point in the season, Mensah's been outstanding with the decision-making and the accuracy; I think Mestemaker is a little more toolsy than him. When we get in draft time, Rich, that's usually what takes the cake."

Eisen and Jeremiah talked about Mestemaker's incredible rise up draft boards into QB1 consideration before Jeremiah added some praise for Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss.

"And I'm a Chambliss guy too. I've been saying that from the jump. He's my favorite one to watch of all these guys. He is so talented and so tough and just such a natural thrower. Like to me, if you said who of all these quarterbacks you've got to win an NFL game tomorrow, like come in and win game one, he's the guy who's most equipped to help you win. He's ready to go."

articles.title: Mike Bianchi: In blowout loss to Louisville, FSU’s Mike Norvell may have outsmarted his way out of a job
articles.summary: Sometimes, one play call changes a game. Sometimes, it changes a season. And sometimes, it changes a coaching career. Mike Norvell may have accomplished all...
articles.body:
Sometimes, one play call changes a game.

And sometimes, it changes a coaching career.

Mike Norvell may have accomplished all three Friday night in Louisville, Ky.

One inexplicable decision. One disastrous swing pass. One historic touchdown run. And perhaps the moment Florida State's embattled football coach officially became a dead man walking.

The final score was Louisville 44, Florida State 20. But the play that may ultimately define Norvell's tenure came when the Seminoles were leading 14-0, dominating the line of scrimmage and threatening to turn this into a blowout of their own.

Florida State had fourth-and-goal at Louisville's 2-yard line.

They had been running the football down Louisville's throat. Quarterback Ashton Daniels had rushed for a school-record five touchdowns the previous week against Virginia. Florida State had piled up nearly 300 rushing yards in that victory.

Smash-mouth football was becoming this team's identity. Finally, something was working.

Instead of putting the ball in Daniels' hands on a run-pass option, instead of challenging Louisville's defense to stop the very thing it hadn't been stopping, Norvell called a little swing pass to true freshman Jasen Lopez.

And, quite possibly, Norvell lost his job.

Because on Louisville's very next offensive snap, Isaac Brown took a handoff and exploded 97 yards for a touchdown.

Just like that, what could have been a commanding 21-0 Florida State lead became 14-7.

A potential knockout punch became an invitation to get off the canvas.

The Cardinals scored 35 unanswered points, transforming what had looked like Florida State's most encouraging performance of the season into another humiliating collapse.

Brown's touchdown was the longest rushing score in college football this season and the longest play from scrimmage ever surrendered by Florida State's defense.

A program once synonymous with speed, intimidation and defensive dominance just surrendered a 97-yard touchdown run that belongs in its record books for all the wrong reasons.

And Brown wasn't finished. He rushed for 235 yards on just 17 carries, including another 68-yard touchdown. Louisville amassed 397 rushing yards, averaging an obscene 9.2 yards per carry.

Brown didn't merely outrun Florida State's defenders. He made them look like traffic cones scattered along a highway, useful only for marking the route to the end zone.

And it started with a coaching decision that defied common sense.

Remember Pete Carroll's infamous Super Bowl blunder? Seattle had the ball at New England's 1-yard line, with Marshawn "Beast Mode" Lynch available to finish the job. Instead, Carroll called a pass that Malcolm Butler intercepted.

A championship opportunity vanished because a coach apparently decided the obvious play wasn't clever enough.

Norvell's decision wasn't made with a Super Bowl championship at stake.

It might have been made with his livelihood at stake.

To be clear, one fourth-down failure didn't cause Louisville to rush for nearly 400 yards. Nor did it excuse Florida State's inability to respond when adversity arrived.

But that's precisely the larger indictment of Norvell. His team couldn't recover.

Good teams absorb bad breaks. Well-coached teams maintain their composure. Teams with strong leadership don't allow one failed offensive play to trigger a complete unraveling.

And this wasn't some isolated road-game nightmare. The Seminoles have now lost 13 consecutive road games.

Winning away from home requires discipline, toughness, preparation and leadership. It requires a team capable of handling momentum swings without disintegrating.

Florida State has demonstrated precious little of that. Which brings us back to Norvell and the cruel reality of coaching on borrowed time.

Just one week earlier, Florida State's domination of Virginia offered a glimmer of hope. Maybe Norvell had finally found an offensive identity. Maybe Daniels' running ability could rescue a season drifting toward irrelevance.

Maybe, just maybe, Norvell could save himself.

Now Florida State is 3-3, with a trip to No. 4 Miami looming. Another blowout would leave the Seminoles at 3-4 and Norvell needing something approaching a miracle finish to preserve his job.

His reported $49 million buyout complicates everything. Florida State's administrators would undoubtedly prefer a resurgence to writing that enormous check. But an increasingly furious fan base doesn't care about contractual complications. It wants results.

And Norvell keeps giving those fans more ammunition.

That's what happens when a coach has exhausted his margin for error. Every loss becomes an indictment. Every questionable decision becomes evidence. Every game becomes a referendum on whether he deserves another one.

Friday night, Florida State had an opportunity to build momentum, establish credibility in the ACC and prove that last week's breakthrough wasn't a mirage.

Instead, the Seminoles squandered a 14-point lead, surrendered a historic touchdown and watched their season veer toward another familiar disaster.

A football season doesn't usually unravel on one play. A coaching career doesn't usually end with one decision.

But sometimes, one moment tells you everything you need to know about a coach and the direction of his program.

Friday night, Florida State had a chance to change the trajectory of its season. Mike Norvell needed just two yards to take a commanding 21-0 lead.

Instead of trusting the running game that had been bulldozing Louisville, he tried to outsmart everybody.

And may have outsmarted himself right out of a job.

Forget the old football adage, "Three yards and a cloud of dust."

For Mike Norvell, this may very well go down as two yards and a cloud of doom.

articles.title: ‘Would Put My Money on Him’ — Ex-USC Star Raves About ‘Freak of Nature’ Jeremiah Smith’s Chances of Winning Heisman Trophy
articles.summary: Matt Leinart believes Jeremiah Smith has shown enough on the field to put himself in the Heisman Trophy conversation. The former USC quarterback has been so...
articles.body:
Matt Leinart believes Jeremiah Smith has shown enough on the field to put himself in the Heisman Trophy conversation. The former USC quarterback has been so impressed by Ohio State's star receiver that he believes Smith could even be the No. 1 overall pick in next year's NFL draft.

Leinart's admiration for Smith dates back to the receiver's freshman season, when he already looked ready to make the jump to the NFL.

Matt Leinart Backs Jeremiah Smith To Win the Heisman

Speaking on "First Things First," Leinart made a strong case for Smith to win college football's most prestigious individual award.

"I would put my money on him winning the Heisman Trophy right now," Leinart said .

Leinart acknowledged that a quarterback could emerge as a Heisman contender. He also stressed the importance of delivering in the biggest games, but remained confident in Smith's chances.

"I think he might end up running away with this thing," Leinart added.

Leinart knows what a Heisman season looks like. He won the award at USC in 2004, finishing ahead of Oklahoma freshman Adrian Peterson.

During the discussion, Leinart recalled Peterson as another young player who made him believe someone could jump directly from high school into the NFL. Smith gave him that same impression almost immediately.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

"From day one, I was like, that dude could be in the NFL tomorrow and be fine. Like, and be good," said the former QB.

Smith's Production Backs Up Leinart's Praise

The Ohio State Buckeyes receiver has backed up the attention with 44 catches for 823 yards and nine touchdowns through five games.

Smith ranks #2 nationally with a PFN CFB WR Impact Score of 96.6, updated Oct. 6. His record-breaking performance against Iowa added another major chapter to a college career already drawing extraordinary comparisons.

Leinart's preferred comparison is Andre Johnson, although he acknowledged that Julio Jones is another name that frequently comes up.

"He's a freak of nature. I'll tell you that," Leinart said.

The conversation also turned to Smith's NFL draft outlook.

Leinart explained that the team holding the No. 1 pick and its quarterback needs would play a role in determining whether a receiver could go first overall. Still, he had little doubt that Smith would be among the first players selected.

"Wherever this guy goes, if he doesn't go one, he's gonna go two or three. There's no doubt about that. He is an absolute stud," Leinart said.

Ohio State hosts Maryland on Saturday, giving Smith another chance to strengthen his Heisman case. Leinart has made his pick. Now, Maryland's secondary will have to find a way to slow Smith down.

articles.title: In 2007, 49ers legend Jerry Rice asked $22 million for his custom-built Silicon Valley mansion; it later sold for $9 million and is now back on the market for $35 million, with 12,520 square feet, Versace floors and Swarovski crystal accents
articles.summary: The French-inspired mansion in California’s Silicon Valley that NFL Hall of Famer Jerry Rice built for himself is back on the market, asking $35 million.
articles.body: The French-inspired mansion in California’s Silicon Valley that NFL Hall of Famer Jerry Rice built for himself is back on the market, asking $35 million. The 49ers legend built the estate at 267 Atherton Ave. in the early 2000s, and it sits on 1.24 acres, according to a report by SFGATE.Built for the NFL GOATThe 49ers legend, who won three Super Bowl titles, used this mansion as his personal residence from 2001 to 2013, according to Mansion Global. This Atherton mansion was a long-term project. It took him years to plan and build.The house, spanning 12,520 square feet, was a major undertaking. Reports from the time say it took years to plan and build, with Rice pushing for exact details throughout. “This is an incredible Atherton estate home that was built with no expense spared in the early 2000s. It was arguably one of the best and most state-of-the-art homes in Atherton at the time of its construction,” listing agent Alex Buljan of Compass told SFGATE.The interiors reflect that effort. Versace limestone floors run throughout the house, and Swarovski crystal accents add extra sparkle to the details.The Juliet balconies, Venetian plastered walls, tall ceilings and exquisite French doors and windows overlooking tranquil gardens are also some of the highlights of the breathtaking mansion."The cleverly laid out estate is hidden inside a peaceful Mediterranean garden imagined by Santana Rows landscape architect," the listing says.The home has six bedrooms and 11 bathrooms, spread across three floors connected by an elevator. The main living areas look out over the grounds, and the central kitchen is large enough for a crowd.The property also has a pool and spa, an outdoor kitchen and dining area, a stone fireplace and a putting green, all designed for entertaining guests. The property also comes with a guest house with its own kitchen.The parking is below ground. The underground garage can accommodate seven cars. Another perk of the mansion is the privacy it offers. Buljan told the outlet that the home is a ‘rare combination of location, privacy and acreage’. “It’s exceptionally private.”A gym built for a footballerAnother highlight of the mansion is its gym. Few sellers keep their workout equipment in the listing, but Rice did. The current listing says his gym still has his gear, along with a sauna.The mansion also comes with a theatre room. It has Art Deco touches and tiered seating. There is a wine cellar with space for 1,000 bottles, as well as a hobby room and a dog run.Meanwhile, the house has not always been easy to sell. Rice first listed the mansion in 2007 for $22 million. The sale took years to close. Earlier reports say a buyer backed out of a deal before the sale went through. Eventually, it was sold for $9 million, less than half the original asking price.After Rice sold the home in 2013, philanthropists Peter and Susanna Pau purchased it. The new $35 million asking price is a big jump from that sale, putting the house in rare company on the Peninsula. articles.title: Examining Week 5 Injury Reports and Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Options
articles.summary: Week 5 opened with one of the bigger surprises of the 2026 NFL season thus far. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers were nearly double-digit underdogs on Thursday night, but they largely dominated the Dallas Cowboys for a huge upset road win.
articles.body:
Week 5 opened with one of the bigger surprises of the 2026 NFL season thus far. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers were nearly double-digit underdogs on Thursday night, but they largely dominated the Dallas Cowboys for a huge upset road win.

Tampa got a huge helping hand from undrafted quarterback Jalon Daniels, who made his second start in place of the injured Baker Mayfield.

Many fantasy managers will be scrambling to find an equally effective injury replacement or two heading into the rest of the schedule. Several notable players will be out, several more are questionable, and the Kansas City Chiefs and Carolina Panthers are both on bye to boot.

Here, we'll dive into the Week 5 injury report , provide rankings for the top remaining point-per-reception (PPR) plays, and highlight some sleepers who may still be available on the waiver wire.

This week's biggest injury news at quarterback is the fact that the Baltimore Ravens have ruled out Lamar Jackson against the Atlanta Falcons because of his ankle injury. Tyler Huntley will get the start in his stead.

The other big news is that Jayden Daniels is expected to return for the Washington Commanders against the New York Giants. Caleb Williams (hamstring) is officially questionable for the Chicago Bears, though fans should prepare for him to miss a third-straight start.

Jacoby Brissett is the top waiver-wire option at quarterback this week, as he has an overwhelmingly favorable matchup. The Arizona Cardinals will host the Detroit Lions, who have surrendered more fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks than any other team.

Brissett is still only rostered in 37 percent of fantasy leagues. Other QBs to consider in Week 5 are Kirk Cousins, Geno Smith, Jameis Winston, and Michael Penix Jr.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

The big news at running back is that the Philadelphia Eagles have officially ruled out Saquon Barkley against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Kyle Monangai is out for the Bears, while Breece Hall will miss another game for the New York Jets.

Ashton Jeanty, Jaylen Wright, Rhamondre Stevenson, Alvin Kamara, and Rico Dowle are among the RBs who are listed as questionable.

Zach Charbonnet is still not ready to make his return for the Seattle Seahawks. With rookie Jadarian Price headed to injured reserve, Emanuel Wilson has some volume value this week, even against a terrific San Francisco 49ers defense.

Of course, Wilson was a very popular add early in the week and is now rostered in 81 percent of leagues. Philadelphia's third back, Will Shipley, is rostered in only 48 percent of leagues and carries similar sleeper value.

The Jags have been good against the run, but with Barkley out and Tank Bigsby on IR, Shipley should see a lot of backfield work this week.

The list of other RBs to consider this week includes Brian Robinson Jr., Kaelon Black, Tyler Allgeier, and Keaton Mitchell.

Minnesota Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson could make his return this week, though he and Jordan Addison are both listed as questionable.

The list of receivers who have already been ruled out includes Adonai Mitchell, Mack Hollins, Michael Pittman Jr., Stefon Diggs, Quentin Johnston, DeVonta Smith, Caleb Douglas, Jalen Nailor, and Tank Dell.

Ladd McConkey, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Carnell Tate, Tim Patrick, Keenan Allen, and Terry McLaurin are among the notable receivers who are listed as questionable.

With Pittman out for an extended period, Pittsburgh Steelers receiver Roman Wilson is a must-add this week. He has topped 13 fantasy points in back-to-back weeks and is still only rostered in 28 percent of fantasy leagues.

Keon Coleman, Tre Tucker, Makai Lemon, Tre Tucker, Tre' Harris, and Chris Bell are other wide receivers to consider adding this week.

The injury list is rather short at tight end, with Charlie Kolar being the only notable name listed as questionable. However, with Travis Kelce and Darren Waller on bye, managers may need alternatives.

With Jefferson and Addison both questionable, Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson is a strong sleeper candidate for Week 5. He's coming off an 18.4-point performance and has a reasonable matchup against a bad New Orleans Saints defense.

The Saints have surrendered an average of 14.3 fantasy points to opposing tight ends this week.

Hockenson is rostered in 55 percent of fantasy leagues, but it's definitely worth checking to see if he's available. If Hockenson can't be snagged, Mike Gesicki, Brenton Strange, Hunter Henry, and Tyler Higbee are solid backup options.
